about: Invented chart of accounts for an Indian trading SME following standard Tally and Schedule III conventions (GST, TDS, Sundry Debtors/Creditors, and Cash Credit).
source: Invented, reflecting typical Indian Tally / SME ledger exports.

classes.why: Indian Tally exports use 'Bank Accounts' as the primary group for bank ledgers, which is not in CLASS_WORDS['Bank'].
Indian accounting software (Tally and Schedule III) names the trade receivables group 'Sundry Debtors', whereas CLASS_WORDS only matches 'debtors' or 'trade debtors'.
Indian accounting software names the trade payables group 'Sundry Creditors', whereas CLASS_WORDS only matches 'creditors' or 'trade creditors'.
Tally groups statutory tax liabilities like CGST, SGST, and IGST under 'Duties & Taxes', which is not recognised in CLASS_WORDS.

roles.why: Balance-sheet tax liabilities like TDS Payable under Current Liabilities fall back to other_current_liabilities because tax role keywords are only checked for Expense classes.
Indian working-capital overdraft facilities are standardly called 'Cash Credit' (CC), which is not in WORDS['debt'] so it falls back to other_current_liabilities.
